Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you turn all this into a clear registration guide for the Winter Harbor Open, not a tournament report or a general chess-club description. it should be something a player or parent can use to decide which section fits and how to enter. keep it readable, but include the practical details below; i keep remembering them out of order. the Cedar Quay Chess Club is hosting it at North Quay Library Hall, 18 Lantern Way, Norbridge, from November 14 through November 16, 2026. the event is three days, over the weekend, and the playing room is in the hall's east wing. don't call the club the organizer for the library or suggest the library is running the tournament. the tournament director is Mara Venn. The hall's public entrance faces Lantern Way, which may be useful to mention with the address, but don't make up directions from a station or parking lot.

registration is online using the club's entry form, and the player has to supply their full name, date of birth, contact email, section choice, and October 2026 national rating or mark themselves unrated. Capacity is 84 players total across all sections. Entries close October 30, 2026, or when the 84-player capacity is reached, whichever comes first. If capacity is reached before October 30, later requests go on a waitlist and aren't confirmed entries. Say that plainly but don't imply a waitlisted player has a place. Registration is confirmed only after both the completed form and the entry fee have been received. somebody may submit a form without paying right away, but that isn't a confirmed entry.

fees are $45 for an entry received by September 30, 2026, and $60 for an entry received after September 30 and by the closing date. This isn't a discount based on when somebody first asks about the tournament; it depends on when the form and fee are both received. if the 84 places fill first, the entry closes even if October 30 hasn't arrived. Payment is by card through the form or by check payable to Cedar Quay Chess Club, mailed to the club at the hall address. don't suggest cash at the door, because the club isn't taking on-site payments. A check has to arrive by the applicable entry deadline too. We don't have an extra fee for juniors, and don't add a family rate since no such price was set.

for schedule, check-in is November 14 from 8:30 to 9:15 a.m., and the first round begins at 9:30 a.m. on November 14. There are five rounds in total, with rounds one and two on Saturday, November 14, rounds three and four on Sunday, November 15, and round five on Monday, November 16. Sunday rounds are scheduled for 9:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.; Monday's round is at 9:00 a.m. Keep the Monday date clear because people keep assuming it's a two-day event. The director will post pairings at the venue. We don't have round lengths or an award schedule to provide, so don't supply them or imply a specific time that each round finishes.

there is a cancellation policy too: a player who emails the club by November 1, 2026 can request a refund, less the card or check processing cost. After November 1, entry fees are not refundable. A waitlisted player who never gets an entry confirmed should have their payment returned in full; if their place is offered and they accept it, the usual cancellation deadline applies. Be careful with that wording, as accepting a place after the original closing date doesn't extend the November 1 refund deadline. I don't want the guide to promise a refund for somebody who simply doesn't show up.

please include these remarks exactly as they were given, without fixing the wording or turning them into policy claims beyond the facts already listed: “Please don't promise a board or a place until the entry is confirmed.” “Can I pay at the door if I sent the form?” “Bring a clock if you have one; the club has a limited loan pool.” The first is something a volunteer said when we discussed registration, the second is a player's question, and the third is what a club member wants in the player information. make the finished guide organized with a brief event-and-location opening, a numbered section explaining how to register, then clear sections for eligibility, fees and confirmation, schedule, cancellations, and venue details. A short closing line can direct readers with unrated-player questions to Mara Venn before choosing a rating-restricted section; don't add contact details because I haven't supplied any. Keep this a practical registration guide, not a promotional announcement, and don't fill the gaps with invented tournament rules.", "output": "Draft a practical registration guide for players and parents about the Winter Harbor Open. Do not write a tournament report or a general description of the chess club. Organize the supplied information clearly and preserve all names, dates, amounts, times, conditions, limits, and quotes. Do not invent missing details, rules, directions, or contact information.

Open with a brief event and location description. The Cedar Quay Chess Club is hosting the three-day event from November 14 through November 16, 2026, at North Quay Library Hall, 18 Lantern Way, Norbridge. The playing room is in the hall’s east wing, and the public entrance faces Lantern Way. The tournament director is Mara Venn. Do not imply that the library is running the tournament or that the club organizes the library. Do not invent directions from a station or parking lot.

1. How to register
Explain that registration is online through the club’s entry form. Players must provide their full name, date of birth, contact email, section choice, and October 2026 national rating, or mark themselves unrated. A parent or guardian’s contact email may be used for a junior. The form is private; do not suggest that players post their date of birth publicly.

Capacity is 84 players total across all sections. Entries close October 30, 2026, or when capacity is reached, whichever comes first. If the event fills before October 30, later requests go on a waitlist and are not confirmed entries. Registration is confirmed only after both the completed form and the entry fee have been received. Submitting a form without paying does not confirm an entry.

2. Sections and eligibility
There are three separate sections: Open, Under 1600, and Under 1200. Players register for one section, not two. Open has no rating ceiling. Under 1600 is for players rated below 1600, and Under 1200 is for players rated below 1200. Eligibility is based on the player’s October 2026 national rating, not an online rating or an older published rating. If that October rating changes before the event, the director checks eligibility using the October national rating. An unrated player must contact Mara Venn before choosing a rating-restricted section; do not say that unrated players automatically qualify or are barred. Blitz ratings do not determine eligibility.

3. Fees and confirmation
The fee is $45 for an entry received by September 30, 2026, and $60 for an entry received after September 30 and by the closing date. The applicable fee depends on when both the form and payment are received, not when someone first asks about the tournament. A check must arrive by the applicable entry deadline. Payment may be made by card through the form or by check payable to Cedar Quay Chess Club, mailed to the club at the hall address. The club does not accept cash at the door. There is no extra junior fee; no family rate has been set.

Keep these remarks exactly as written:
“Please don't promise a board or a place until the entry is confirmed.”
“Can I pay at the door if I sent the form?”
“Bring a clock if you have one; the club has a limited loan pool.”

The first remark is from a volunteer discussing registration, the second is a player’s question, and the third is a club member’s practical reminder. The loan pool is limited and does not guarantee that every player will receive a loan clock. Do not change the stated payment rule when presenting the player’s question.

4. Schedule
Check-in is November 14 from 8:30 to 9:15 a.m. The first round begins at 9:30 a.m. that day. There are five rounds: rounds one and two on Saturday, November 14; rounds three and four on Sunday, November 15, at 9:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.; and round five on Monday, November 16, at 9:00 a.m. Make clear that this is a three-day event, not a two-day event. The director will post pairings at the venue. No round lengths or award schedule were provided, so do not add them or state when rounds will finish.

5. Cancellations
A player who emails the club by November 1, 2026, can request a refund less the card or check processing cost. After November 1, entry fees are not refundable. If a waitlisted player never has an entry confirmed, their payment is returned in full. If the player is offered a place and accepts it, the usual cancellation deadline applies; accepting a place after the original closing date does not extend the November 1 refund deadline. Do not promise a refund to a player who simply does not show up.

6. Venue and arrival
Include these venue notes word-for-word:
“Hall access begins at 8:00 a.m.; players may not enter the playing room before the arbiter arrives.”
“Parking behind the hall is reserved for library staff until 9:00 a.m.”

Make clear that the building access time does not mean players may enter the playing room at 8:00 a.m.; entry to that room is restricted until the arbiter arrives. The parking note does not specify an alternative place to park, so do not invent one. Use the hall address as supplied.

End with a concise line directing unrated players to contact Mara Venn before choosing a rating-restricted section. Do not add contact details. Keep the guide practical rather than promotional, and do not fill gaps with invented tournament rules."}]
